description:
Reproduced 2026-09-14 at main f26264572 on interp, run and build:

    def main() do
      n = 2
      take = fn <<s::binary-size(n), _::binary>> -> s end
      dbg(take.("hello"))
    end

Elixir prints "he" (n is in the lambda's prematch snapshot; 1.20 warns that it should be pinned as size(^n)). fz: error[lower/unbound]: compiler2 lowering found unbound bit size name `n` (single clause) or "compiler2 local dispatch pinned name `n` is unresolved" (multi-clause).

Cause: collect_pattern_free_names (src/compiler2/jobs/body.rs ~4667-4671) recurses into a bitstring field's value and never inspects its size expression, so a size variable never becomes a capture, never becomes an input of the lambda, and never lands in env. The fix is one arm: a size name that no earlier field binds is a free name of the pattern. After fz-acn.2 binds pins from the prematch, the captured n then binds like any other pin.

Signal: the program above on three doors with an oracle twin; the same shape with size(^n) once the parser accepts a pin inside size.
title: A lambda whose bitstring size names a captured variable fails to compile
